interpretation.summary: A Welch independent two-group t-test compared the mean outcome between the treatment and control groups, with the contrast expressed as treatment minus control. The estimated mean difference was 1.2674, with a ninety-five percent confidence interval from 0.82116 to 1.7136, based on 49 observations. The associated p-value was 8.328e-07, which is below the five percent threshold, so the evidence is classified as evidence of a group difference in means. The interval lies entirely above zero, indicating the treatment group mean is higher than the control group mean in this sample. Because the design is observational, this result describes an association or group difference only and does not establish that the group assignment produced the difference. One observation was excluded through complete-case deletion, and missingness may bias the results. Welch's method does not require equal variances, but independence of observations is assumed and was user-confirmed rather than verified from the data.
limitations: This analysis does not establish causality.
